newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil rebound.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil rebound.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil and gas oil swaps market rebounded late afternoon on Wednesday on profit-taking and a technical correction to the recent price collapse, traders said.
"There is a slight rebound mainly because of some profit-taking by traders who had sold earlier," one broker said.
Gas oil swaps traded firmer with February deals seen at up to a high of $25.50 per barrel, compared with Tuesday's $25.10/$25.30.
Earlier in the day, the market traded at $25.25, 25.28 and 25.35 per barrel, brokers said.
February was last quoted at $25.50/$25.70, they said.
March was quoted at $25.80/$26.00, up from Monday's $25.40/$25.60 with the February/March contango unchanged at minus 50/30 cents.
Traders said the contango needed to widen for people to buy prompt cargoes.
Some traders said the market might weaken late in the day as physical sellers emerge for both gas oil and fuel oil.
In the past two weeks, physical gas oil prices in Singapore have slumped more than $6.00 per barrel, or about 20 percent, while fuel oil has lost around $28 per tonne, or 22 percent.
"It's not clear if anyone would come out to buy any of the prompt physical (gas oil and fuel oil) cargoes," a trader said.
February fuel oil swaps firmed in the afternoon and were last quoted up $2.00 per tonne from Monday at $97.00/$98.00, one broker said.
The market traded at $97.00 per tonne up from a traded low of $95.50 a tonne on Monday night, one broker said.
March offers were quoted at $98.00/$99.00 per tonne, also up $2.00 from Tuesday. March traded in the afternoon at $97.75 a tonne, brokers said.
